introduction_raw:
If your car or truck won't start, it may be time to change the battery. A typical motor vehicle battery lasts about 3-4 years, but this lifespan can vary greatly depending on the conditions and your driving habits.

This guide uses a Toyota Corolla to demonstrate the procedure, which is similar to most common motor vehicles.

If you just need to temporarily disconnect the battery rather than remove or replace it, [guide|66802|follow this shorter guide.]

***Warning***: Modern vehicles with a start-stop system often have a battery management system (BMS) that makes it necessary to pair the battery with special equipment after a replacement. A disconnected battery can cause infotainment, powered windows, and other vehicle electronics to lose their settings and require re-initialization. In some cases, error codes must also be resolved. Consult your owner's manual for details.

lines.text_raw: Before you begin, switch the ignition '''off''' and remove the key.
lines.text_rendered: Before you begin, switch the ignition off and remove the key.

lines.text_raw: Make sure the transmission is in Park (or first gear if you have a manual gearbox) and that the parking brake is engaged.
lines.text_rendered: Make sure the transmission is in Park (or first gear if you have a manual gearbox) and that the parking brake is engaged.

lines.text_raw: Put on work gloves and safety goggles if you have them available.

lines.text_raw: In addition to being dirty, the battery contains corrosive agents and may release flammable gases.

lines.text_raw: Gloves can also help protect you from an unpleasant shock if you accidentally mishandle the battery.

lines.text_raw: ''Most motor vehicle batteries are located in the engine bay, under the hood (a.k.a. bonnet). If your battery is located elsewhere, '''[https://www.ifixit.com/Guide/How+to+Disconnect+a+Car+or+Truck+Battery/66802#s136007|skip to Step 5].''' ''
lines.text_rendered: Most motor vehicle batteries are located in the engine bay, under the hood (a.k.a. bonnet). If your battery is located elsewhere, skip to Step 5.

lines.text_raw: ''If you're not sure, simply continue reading.''
lines.text_rendered: If you're not sure, simply continue reading.

lines.text_raw: Pull the hood release lever. It's usually located inside the car, near the steering wheel.

lines.text_raw: Raise the hood by simultaneously lifting and pressing up on the hood latch release (usually located beneath the front edge of the hood, near the center or center-right).

lines.text_raw: At this point, depending on the vehicle, your hood may raise and support itself automatically.
lines.text_rendered: At this point, depending on the vehicle, your hood may raise and support itself automatically.

lines.text_raw: If not, use one hand to hold the hood open temporarily while securing the hood with the prop rod:
lines.text_rendered: If not, use one hand to hold the hood open temporarily while securing the hood with the prop rod:

lines.text_raw: Lift one end of the prop rod up or out to release it from the front area of the engine bay.
lines.text_rendered: Lift one end of the prop rod up or out to release it from the front area of the engine bay.

lines.text_raw: Swing the end of the prop rod up and slide it into the cutout on the underside of the hood.
lines.text_rendered: Swing the end of the prop rod up and slide it into the cutout on the underside of the hood.

lines.text_raw: Make sure the hood is well secured before you let go with your other hand, or it may fall and injure you.
lines.text_rendered: Make sure the hood is well secured before you let go with your other hand, or it may fall and injure you.

lines.text_raw: Locate the battery. It's normally rectangular and roughly 8-14" across.
lines.text_rendered: Locate the battery. It's normally rectangular and roughly 8-14" across.

lines.text_raw: The battery may be easy to spot, or it may lie under a plastic cover—usually marked with positive (+) and/or negative (-) symbols.
lines.text_rendered: The battery may be easy to spot, or it may lie under a plastic cover—usually marked with positive (+) and/or negative (-) symbols.

lines.text_raw: On some models, the battery may be located in the trunk—usually under or behind the trunk lining. Look around or consult your owner's manual.
lines.text_rendered: On some models, the battery may be located in the trunk—usually under or behind the trunk lining. Look around or consult your owner's manual.

lines.text_raw: Using a correctly sized wrench or socket, loosen the nut/bolt securing the cable on the '''negative''' battery terminal.
lines.text_rendered: Using a correctly sized wrench or socket, loosen the nut/bolt securing the cable on the negative battery terminal.

lines.text_raw: Always disconnect the negative cable '''first''' (before removing the positive cable).
lines.text_rendered: Always disconnect the negative cable first (before removing the positive cable).

lines.text_raw: The negative terminal may be marked with a minus (-) symbol, or it may be unmarked. The positive terminal is almost always marked with a plus (+) symbol, often in red.
lines.text_rendered: The negative terminal may be marked with a minus (-) symbol, or it may be unmarked. The positive terminal is almost always marked with a plus (+) symbol, often in red.

lines.text_raw: If the nut or bolt spins without loosening, it may be necessary to counter-hold the opposite side with a second wrench or socket.
lines.text_rendered: If the nut or bolt spins without loosening, it may be necessary to counter-hold the opposite side with a second wrench or socket.

comments.title: How to Disconnect a Car or Truck Battery
comments.text_raw: Make sure to use a power/computer memory saver for newer car model before disconnecting the car battery.  This should be done to prevent losing all your settings, radio stations etc.
comments.text_rendered: Make sure to use a power/computer memory saver for newer car model before disconnecting the car battery. This should be done to prevent losing all your settings, radio stations etc.

lines.text_raw: Remove the cable from the negative battery terminal.
lines.text_rendered: Remove the cable from the negative battery terminal.

lines.text_raw: When connecting the battery, it is advised to roughen up the battery terminals and clean the cable clamp beforehand.
lines.text_rendered: When connecting the battery, it is advised to roughen up the battery terminals and clean the cable clamp beforehand.

lines.text_raw: Upon reconnecting the battery, make sure to seal the pole connections with an appropriate terminal grease or terminal spray.
lines.text_rendered: Upon reconnecting the battery, make sure to seal the pole connections with an appropriate terminal grease or terminal spray.

lines.text_raw: Prevent the cable from making accidental contact with the terminal by pushing it aside and/or wrapping the cable clamp with a dry rag.
lines.text_rendered: Prevent the cable from making accidental contact with the terminal by pushing it aside and/or wrapping the cable clamp with a dry rag.

lines.text_raw: Remove the insulating cover from the positive battery terminal (if one is present).
lines.text_rendered: Remove the insulating cover from the positive battery terminal (if one is present).

lines.text_raw: Using a correctly sized wrench or socket, loosen the nut/bolt securing the cable on the '''positive''' battery terminal.
lines.text_rendered: Using a correctly sized wrench or socket, loosen the nut/bolt securing the cable on the positive battery terminal.

lines.text_raw: If the nut or bolt spins without loosening, it may be necessary to counter-hold the opposite side with a second wrench or socket.
lines.text_rendered: If the nut or bolt spins without loosening, it may be necessary to counter-hold the opposite side with a second wrench or socket.

lines.text_raw: Remove the cable from the positive battery terminal.
lines.text_rendered: Remove the cable from the positive battery terminal.

lines.text_raw: During reassembly, be sure to reconnect and tighten the positive cable clamp '''first''' (before the negative cable clamp).
lines.text_rendered: During reassembly, be sure to reconnect and tighten the positive cable clamp first (before the negative cable clamp).

lines.text_raw: Remove any bolts securing the battery.
lines.text_rendered: Remove any bolts securing the battery.

lines.text_raw: Remove any bars or brackets securing the battery.
lines.text_rendered: Remove any bars or brackets securing the battery.

lines.text_raw: Remove the battery.
lines.text_rendered: Remove the battery.

lines.text_raw: A typical car battery can weigh 50 pounds or more, so lift carefully and get help if needed. Do ***not*** drop the battery, as this can release dangerous chemicals.
lines.text_rendered: A typical car battery can weigh 50 pounds or more, so lift carefully and get help if needed. Do not drop the battery, as this can release dangerous chemicals.

lines.text_raw: If your battery cable clamps look dirty and/or corroded, clean them up with a wire brush and a mixture of water and baking soda before installing your new battery.
lines.text_rendered: If your battery cable clamps look dirty and/or corroded, clean them up with a wire brush and a mixture of water and baking soda before installing your new battery.

lines.text_raw: To prevent corrosion in the future, coat the new battery's terminals with a little dielectric grease or petroleum jelly.
lines.text_rendered: To prevent corrosion in the future, coat the new battery's terminals with a little dielectric grease or petroleum jelly.

lines.text_raw: ***Don't throw the old battery in the trash.*** Many auto parts stores and service stations will accept old batteries for free safe disposal.
lines.text_rendered: Don't throw the old battery in the trash. Many auto parts stores and service stations will accept old batteries for free safe disposal.

comments.text_raw: To prevent future corrosion, apply some vaseline to the terminals after the re-installation of the battery. The engine heat will help spread it into all the nooks & crannies that you think you might have missed.
